newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian dlr makes hard work of modest rally.
newsitem.headline: Australian dlr makes hard work of modest rally.

text.p: The Australian dollar faded back toward 75 cents at the midsession as a flurry of AUD/yen sales out of Tokyo sapped some of its early bluster.

Encouraged by a short covering bounce from US$0.7470 support offshore, speculators bought at the opening in the hope of triggering stops atop US$0.7520. But a huge rise in the Japanese trade surplus roiled US$/yen and the A$ ran into heavy offers at 85.30 which lopped over 1/2 yen off it in minutes.
The resulting pullback found support at 75 cents and US$/yen proved resilient, if choppy, allowing the A$ to stabilise, and dealers reckoned a period of consolidation lay ahead.
By 12.00 pm (0200 GMT) the local dollar was hovering at US$0.7504/09 having been quoted as high as US$0.7522, but was still ahead of Tuesday's late US$0.7480/85.
Analysts said sentiment remained bearish on both a technical and yield differential view and the currency needed to clear US$0.7535 resistance soon to avoid another date with the downside.

Support around US$0.7475 had impressed overnight with bids coming from corporate, U.S. and Swiss sources. But most still favoured an eventual test of US$0.7450 and saw a real risk of a return to the 1996 low of 73 cents in the next couple of months.
On the crosses activity was more than a little confused after the release of Japanese trade data showing its surplus soared 222 percent to 738.27 billion yen in May.
This was well above median market forecasts of 592 billion but appeared to have been not as bad as some feared since US$/yen rallied in its wake.

The U.S. currency did turn lower when a U.S. official was quoted saying the data reinforced U.S. concerns that Japan's surplus seemed to be rising again. Signs of trade tensions tend to depress the dollar since the market has suspected the U.S. of using currency depreciation as a trade weapon in the past.
The dollar fell as far as 112.80 immediately afterwards but quickly bounced to 113.25/35 to be little changed on the day.
The local currency followed to stand at 84.95/05, down from a 85.35 high but up on Tuesday's 84.64/74 finish.
In trade weighted terms the dollar edged up to 56.8 from a previous 56.7 close.

There were no domestic data of note due today and little out until May retail trade on July 2, which had convinced many dealers the Reserve Bank would make no move on rates until its monthly board meeting on July 1 at the earliest.
